name: Kill Holiday
label: Revelation
lede: Two members of San Diego's Unbroken swapped metallic hardcore for long, moody indie rock and left behind four records, one of them a seven-minute-song album on Revelation.

eras.title: An Unbroken side road
eras.text: Unbroken were one of San Diego's heaviest hardcore bands. Kill Holiday was two of its members, Steven Miller and Rob Moran, going somewhere else entirely, with every early single cut at Doubletime Studio with engineer Jeff Forrest.

years.h: Unbroken's Steve Miller and Rob Moran start Kill Holiday
years.p: Steven Miller sings and plays guitar, Rob Moran plays bass, with Oscar Paz on guitar and Barry Kellman on drums. The band plays indie rock and punk, not Unbroken's metallic hardcore.
Recorded in one day, March 27, 1995, at Doubletime Studio with Jeff Forrest. Two songs: Monitor Dependency and Cold Shoulder.

years.h: Kill Holiday split a 7" with Dempsey on Indecision
years.p: Agenda and Sugar Rush share a 7" with Dempsey on Indecision Records: 274 on yellow vinyl, 353 on black. Rob Moran is gone; June Cate is in.

years.h: Meant To Let You Down 7" on Simba
years.p: Recorded July 20, 1997, with Todd Beattie on bass. [[Gabriel Gamboa|bc189271-5c40-40e0-bcd5-0f29cfa1c6f7]] shoots the photos and does the layout, a year before he takes over the drums.

eras.title: Seven-minute songs on Revelation
eras.text: Kill Holiday's only album stretched out: ten songs, several past seven minutes, with keyboards and noise. It came out on Revelation in 1999, and the band was finished the next year.

years.h: Kill Holiday record their album at Doubletime
years.p: Steven Miller, Christopher Perreira on guitar, Todd Beattie and Gabriel Gamboa, now drumming, cut the album with Jeff Forrest, who adds keyboards and noises.

years.h: Somewhere Between the Wrong Is Right · Revelation Rev:77
years.p: Ten songs, with You're Taking It Well, Something Borrowed Something Blue and In Closing (Memorial Day) all over seven minutes. [[Jeff Caudill|6a41fff4-9b5c-4b1c-9ebf-4df434fdbbec]] of [[Gameface|c67fddd4-970b-4bfb-8996-314c29b08f27]] shot the cover and designed it.
play: Somewhere Between the Wrong Is Right

years.p: After six years and four releases, Kill Holiday end in 2000. Miller and Gamboa carry on together in [[The Landslide|12c8eb9a-bcef-4cae-a45b-9861c41705b9]]; Moran later plays in [[Some Girls|ffee2206-eb9e-4b39-9447-8977e269ed0e]] and [[Narrows|3a9bf775-66f1-4299-b062-5cb0585d5672]].

eras.title: Purple for Record Store Day
eras.text: Revelation brought the album back on vinyl for collectors seventeen years later.

years.h: Somewhere Between the Wrong Is Right on purple vinyl
years.p: A Record Store Day 2016 pressing from Revelation: 717 copies on purple vinyl, with a lyric and credits sheet.
